Marissa / team — ran a quick engineering pass against the MOP. High-level procurement + validation timeline (conservative):

OEM (Galaxy) hardware procurement: 16–20 weeks from PO to delivered racks (current quoted lead time; see attached oem_quote_galaxy_10k.xlsx).
Rack integration + burn-in: 2 weeks.
Image bake/validation (Redwood runtime, perf testing at p95): 2–3 weeks (depends on model repo size).
Network provisioning / tenancy carveout: 1 week.
Total (PO -> healthy Dedicated serving): ~21–26 weeks.

Given those numbers, Jan 15 target is only feasible if we: 1) already have committed capacity in our pipeline that can be reallocated, or 2) use cloud-reserved instances (Helium or similar) for an 8–10 week bridge while OEM fulfillment completes.

Technical fallback plan (recommended):
- Phase A (Week 0–6): Reserved cloud capacity for 40–60 GPUs (Helium). Configure identical runtime images and KV cache settings so client-facing behaviour is identical.
- Phase B (Week 6–14): Incremental Dedicated shipments (if OEM can split shipment) — receive first 40–60 GPUs, run in hybrid mode.
- Phase C (Week 14+): Full Dedicated pool owned by Acme. We’ll run a controlled cutover with canary routes and automatic fallback to cloud.

Risk notes and mitigations: 
- OEM single-shipment risk — push for split-shipment terms in PO.
- Quarantine for component shortages — we can accept partial ship dates in contract.
- Cost: cloud bridge will add ~22–35% unit cost vs committed Dedicated; provide line items in PO.

Attachments: oem_quote_galaxy_10k.xlsx (detailed ETA and per-unit pricing).

Dev — can you confirm whether Redwood’s existing reserved-pool quotas have any soft capacity that we could repurpose immediately (short-term loan) and the lead time to switch back?

- Rishi
